# FURUNCLES AND CARBUNCLES

Localized purulent infections include furuncles, carbuncles and cutaneous abscesses. Nearly all are caused by Staphylococcus aureus. A furuncle is an inflamed nodule that usually develops as a complication of folliculitis. A carbuncle is a more extensive lesion that extends further into the subcutaneous tissue. Contact a wound care nurse for more information.
Incision and drainage is the mainstay of therapy for carbuncles, cutaneous abscesses, and large furuncles.
The decision to administer antibiotics directed against S. aureus as an adjunct to incision and drainage should be made based on the presence of systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) or in patients with markedly impaired host defenses.

## For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy recommended consider a decolonization regimen.

Refer to the outpatient or inpatient Skin Infection section of the Antimicrobial CDSS for recommendations.

## Mild infection: Purulent infection without systemic signs of infection

Recommend incision and drainage. No antibiotic indicated.

## Moderate Infection: Purulent infection with signs of systemic infection.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide therapy.
Treat for 5 days and extend/modify treatment if not improved in this time.

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Preferred treatment:

Cephalexin 500 mg PO q6h ($) [R]

Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) R,DI

### Alternative:

Doxycycline 100 mg po q12h ($) DI
Clindamycin 300 mg PO q6h ($) [H,O]

### If methicillin-RESISTANT Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected or proved

Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) DI

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) R,DI

### Severe Infections:

Patients who have failed incision and drainage along with oral antibiotics or those with SIRS or for infections in those with neutropenia or diminished neutrophil function.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide therapy.

Treat for 5 days. Reevaluate patient and extend or modify treatment if not improved in this time.

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R

## Outpatient

### Preferred treatment

Cephalexin 500 mg po qid for 5 days ($) [R] >
Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid ($) R,DI

### Alternatives

Doxycycline 100 mg po BID ($) DI

Clindamycin 300 mg PO qid for 5 days ($) [H]
### If methicillin-RESISTANT Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected or proved

Doxycycline 100 mg po BID ($) DI

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID ($) R,DI

Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 5 days ($) DI,O

### Severe Infections:

Patients who have failed incision and drainage along with oral antibiotics or those with SIRS or for infections in those with neutropenia or diminished neutrophil function.

See Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

## ER/UC

### Preferred treatment

Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO bid for 5 days ($) R

< OR >
Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid ($) R,DI

### Alternatives

Doxycycline 100 mg po BID ($) DI

### If methicillin-RESISTANT Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected or proved

Doxycycline 100 mg po BID ($) DI

< OR >
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID ($) R,DI

### Severe Infections:

Patients who have failed incision and drainage along with oral antibiotics or those with SIRS or for infections in those with neutropenia or diminished neutrophil function.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide therapy.

Treat for 5 days. Reevaluate patient and extend or modify treatment if not improved in this time.

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV once STAT ($) [R]

*Local guidance (Omaha CDSS, ER/UC):*
Cephalexin 500 mg po qid for 5 days ($) [R]
Clindamycin 300 mg PO qid for 5 days ($) [H]
